subject: Regional p95 variability: US-EAST capacity pool contention — customer update
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@aurorabiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Regional p95 variability: US-EAST capacity pool contention — customer update

Hi Alex,

I wanted to reach out proactively about a short outage/latency event we saw this morning affecting the generate and chat endpoints for customers routed to our US-EAST region. Summary: between ~08:00 and 09:05 ET we observed elevated p95/p99 latencies for a subset of traffic. The immediate customer impact was transient request elongation on long-sequence generation jobs (clients saw spikes in tail latency and a small number of timed-out requests).

What happened (short version): an autoscaler race during a sudden scheduling burst caused contention in the local capacity pool. That contention increased queueing in our serving runtime and surfaced as higher tail latency for affected tokens. Our automated fallback routing moved impacted requests to the warm standby pool at 08:43 ET which reduced failures but introduced higher token latencies until we completed a targeted scale-up at 09:05 ET.

What we did:
- Detected anomaly at 08:07 ET via p95 alerting and token queue depth metrics.
- Engaged on-call and increased routing to cold/warm pools to avoid failed requests (08:43 ET).
- Applied targeted pool scale-up and adjusted scheduler timeouts (09:05 ET) which returned p95 within normal bounds by 09:12 ET.

Customer impact:
- Brief p95/p99 latency elevation (median unaffected).
- Small number of timeouts for very long sequences (we estimate <0.05% of requests for affected tenancies).

Immediate ask: if you have any examples of requests that still show issues, could you forward request ids or a minimal repro? We'll prioritize those. We've attached a short timeline and the mitigation diff.

Next steps: we are drafting a post-incident timeline and a permanent scheduler fix; I'll share the postmortem and the status page incident link once ready.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final update: US-EAST capacity pool event — timeline & postmortem link

Hi Alex — following up with the full incident summary and links. Thank you for the logs you sent earlier; they helped confirm the worst-affected request paths.

Summary and links:
- Root cause: autoscaler race during high-scheduling burst which led to transient pool contention and elevated token queueing.
- Mitigation applied: routing to warm standby (08:43 ET) + targeted scale-up (09:05 ET).
- Residual impact: short-lived p95/p99 elevation; request timeouts limited to a very small subset.
- Permanent fix: scheduler and autoscaler race condition PR submitted (internal PR #4621) and scheduled for staged rollout next week after additional testing.

Postmortem: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/ops/postmortems/UE-20261005 (internal)
Status page incident: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/UE-2026-10-05

Attachments: us-east_incident_timeline_20261005.pdf (timeline), mitigation_patch.diff (patch outline).

If Aurora would like a short 30-minute technical walkthrough of the timeline and the planned fix, we can schedule a session tomorrow — let me know preferred times.

Thanks again for the quick cooperation.

Best,
